title: Parallax Conformance Adapter Output
description: JSON output emitted by a language implementation conformance adapter. The adapter is the `m-conformance-adapter` seam used by external runners to ask a concrete language implementation what it supports, what SQL it emits for a compatibility case, and what observations it produces when it runs a case.

storedDataRecord.description: One result position a read classified rather than published as itself. `ordinal` is its zero-based place in the ordered result, `hydrated` states whether the normative collapse produced a value at that position, and `issues` is the deduplicated diagnosis set the position carries.

storedDataIssue.description: One stored-data violation: its closed `code`, the canonical `entity` it was found on, the dotted `member` path where one is nameable, and the affected `objectKey` where the object's own identity decoded.

profileName.description: The stable reporting name of a declared database matrix profile (`database-provider-test-contract.md`), such as `pg-full`. It names an adapter configuration rather than a dialect: two profiles may execute in the same dialect, and the dialect a profile runs in is read back off the adapter it declares.

caseTag.description: A compatibility case tag from a case's `tags` array.

caseTagClaims.description: Optional tag filters that narrow broad module/case-shape claims. `include` means a case must have at least one listed tag; `exclude` means a case with any listed tag is outside the claim.

bindValue.description: A JSON-serializable bind value. A modeled value is emitted in m-wire canonical form for its resolved NeutralType; dialect-native control binds retain their SQL/dialect contract. Objects and arrays are allowed for structured-document values.

row.description: A logical observed row. Every modeled scalar leaf uses m-wire canonical output for its resolved declaration; declared Value Object documents apply that rule recursively.

stateCheck.description: A lifecycle-state observation (m-conformance-adapter): the object at case position `at` was observed in a given lifecycle state, and `pass` records whether that matched the case's `expectState`. `at` is a JSON Pointer into the case (a scenario step index). Mirrors `identityCheck`'s explicit-verdict shape so the runner grades an assertion the wire golden SQL cannot see.

errorObservation.description: A raised-application-error observation (m-conformance-adapter): the verb at case position `at` raised the neutral application-lifecycle error `errorClass`, from the closed vocabulary the case's `expectError` names (m-detach / m-identity-map / m-unit-work). Distinct from the m-db-error taxonomy; `native` optionally carries the implementation's raw error payload as an unconstrained witness.

stepRowsObservation.description: The values ONE scenario read step published (m-conformance-adapter): `at` is the JSON Pointer naming the step, and `rows` the roots that read handed over, in the physically-keyed shape a whole-read `rows` observation carries and a step's `expectRows` is authored in. What is reported is what the step PUBLISHED, never the result sets its statements returned: a deep fetch's child levels return rows belonging under the roots rather than beside them, and a streamed step returns one result set per page while publishing one root at a time, so its entry is the roots of the whole delivery in delivery order. The resolving read of a materializing predicate write reports no entry — that read is the write's own internal resolve, which hands its rows to no caller.

stepGraphObservation.description: The relationship contents observed at ONE scenario step declaring `expectGraph` (m-case-format): `at` is the JSON Pointer naming the step, and `graph` the contents that step observed. The observable's two placements report two different graphs. An ACCESS step reports what the already-materialized view it navigates still holds, keyed by the traversed relationship's target Entity under its local name — never a re-read, since an adapter that re-queries reports that the database is right while the case asks whether the view survived. A READ step reports what that read itself materialized, roots and included relationships together, keyed by its own target Entity — the same value a whole-read `graph` observation carries, reported per step because a scenario has many reads.

graph.description: A logical object graph whose modeled scalar leaves use m-wire canonical output. Opaque Json values are not recursively assigned inferred NeutralTypes.

milestoneGraphObservation.description: One edge-pinned graph in the ordered observation for a milestone-set snapshot read. The pin is the milestone's own from-instant per as-of axis, keyed by as-of attribute name; graph has the same root-class-keyed shape as a single graph observation.

lifecycleTarget.description: The Entity an observed activity names, in the same Entity-name grammar the case oracle authors — a target an adapter reports is the canonical spelling its own metamodel resolved. The grammar is COPIED from `identity.schema.json`, which this self-contained envelope does not reach; the harness pins the copy against the canonical definition so the two cannot drift.

lifecycleRoot.description: One normalized Root Execution (m-execution-lifecycle): one outermost Handle operation and everything it causally contains. `execution` replaces the runtime UUIDv4 with a positive FIRST-OBSERVATION index, which orders concurrent roots without stating an identity no run reproduces. `kind` names which outermost operation opened it. `events` is the delivered stream in delivery order, a failed activity's transitions included: a Started and its Finished are the same activity delivered twice, so the shortest possible root holds two.

lifecycleEvent.description: One delivered transition: the correlation envelope every event carries, plus EXACTLY ONE concrete transition wrapper naming what happened. `sequence` is the one-based contiguous delivery position within the root and `activity` the one-based contiguous ID a Started assigns and its Finished reuses, so the two deliberately disagree. `parent` is the Activity ID containing this one and is `null` on the root activity ALONE — authored rather than omitted, because "this activity is the root" is the assertion. The wrapper is the same closed-union idiom the rest of this schema uses: naming the transition is what keeps a reader from telling two transitions apart by which fields happen to be present.

lifecycleNoFields.description: A transition whose payload is its correlation alone. A Transaction Attempt names no attempt-specific field, because which attempt of the invocation it is reads off the envelope and everything about the policy it runs under was stated by the invocation that opened it; a Stream Batch names none for the same reason about the stream that opened it.

lifecycleReadStarted.description: A Read opened over `target` through `interface`, after public preflight and after any read-dependency Write Batch. `interface` is the public read interface that publishes the result — `typed`, `wire`, or the internal `rows` values lane — which is what distinguishes two reads of one Entity differing only in what they materialize.

lifecycleWriteBatchStarted.description: A nonempty unit-of-work buffer is being flushed, naming the CLOSED `m-unit-work` trigger that produced it: `read-dependency` for the batch a dependent read forced — which finishes before the Read it enabled starts — or `pre-commit` for the boundary-owned final batch. An empty buffer emits nothing at all, so a batch in the stream always had something to write.

lifecycleDatabaseCallStarted.description: One attempted round trip is about to run. `statement` is the zero-based index into this envelope's own `emissions` array — the call names the statement it ran rather than repeating its SQL or binds, which is what keeps `then.statements` the sole SQL and bind oracle — and is omitted where `emissions` holds no statement to name: an envelope reporting no emission at all (an `api-conformance` case), where `kind` and the outcome are the whole portable oracle, and the resolving read a keyed write owes, which `roundTrips` counts and no emission states. The indexes the remaining calls name are the emission order exactly, in delivery order and once each. `kind` keeps a FAILED call classifiable without parsing SQL. The index rides Started alone: its Finished peer is the same activity, so repeating it would state one fact twice.

lifecycleDatabaseCallFinished.description: The round trip came back, however it came back — a CLOSED union of exactly one outcome. `readCompleted` carries the PHYSICAL row count the statement returned, never a count of result roots, unique graph nodes, or projection views; `writeCompleted` the affected-row count, which is a COMPLETION even when it falls short of what the step addressed. `failed` carries the neutral `m-db-error` category the failure classified to, `null` where it classified to none — the ONE place a category is portable at all, because a failed Database Call is the one activity carrying a Database Failure Diagnostic, and begin, commit, and rollback are no Database Call. The monotonic duration, the message, the native code, and the raised type are not portable and are absent.

allOf.description: Each outcome admits its own payload and no other's. Keying the payload on the outcome is what makes this a closed algebra rather than three independent optional fields, so a row count can never stand beside a failure.

lifecycleInvocationStarted.description: One call to callback demarcation opened, as exactly one of the two invocation kinds. An `outer` invocation opened the boundary and is therefore the root activity, so it states the RESOLVED Concurrency Preference and retry policy it runs under — resolved values only, never whether the caller supplied them — plus the Isolation Level it REQUESTED, which has no resolved form above the port: a boundary naming no level runs at whatever the adapter defaults to, so `isolation` is stated when one was named and absent otherwise rather than reporting a default nothing here established. A `joined` invocation shares the outer root, unit of work, and transaction, runs no Transaction Attempt of its own, and states none of the four: all were resolved by the invocation it joined, which a joined boundary may not renegotiate.

allOf.description: The resolved policy belongs to the invocation that resolved it: an outer invocation states all three, and a joined one states none, because restating an inherited value would read as a renegotiation. The requested isolation is OPTIONAL on an outer invocation — a boundary may name none — and forbidden on a joined one for the same reason the other three are.

lifecycleInvocationFinished.description: The invocation reached its terminal outcome, a CLOSED union of exactly one member. `committed` and `failed` belong to an OUTER invocation and describe the physical boundary; `returned` and `raised` belong to a JOINED one and describe the nested callback ALONE, never claiming the physical transaction committed or rolled back.

lifecycleActivityOutcome.description: A Read, Write Batch, or Stream Batch reached its terminal outcome: `completed` or `failed`. A Write Batch that planning reduced to zero DML completes exactly like one that ran statements — the buffer was spent either way — and a Read completes when its public result is ready.

lifecycleAttemptFinished.description: One physical attempt reached its terminal outcome. `committed` ends the invocation. `rolledBack` and `rollbackFailed` carry the Attempt Failure: `phase` locates it inside the attempt — `callback` (the callback and everything it caused, joined invocations and read-dependency batches included), `pre-commit` (the boundary-owned final batch), `commit` (the durability call) — without exposing a stack location or an internal planner stage, and `retryEligible` is the CLASSIFIER's verdict under the effective policy, independent of the remaining budget and claiming nothing about whether another attempt occurred. `rollbackFailed` additionally admits `rollbackCode`, the stable code of the SECOND live failure, prefixed because two failures collide on one event.

allOf.description: A committed attempt carries no failure: stating one beside `committed` states two outcomes for one attempt.
Only a FAILED rollback names a second failure's code: an attempt whose rollback completed has one live failure and reports one.
A `commit`-phase failure names no cause. The durability boundary is no Database Call and opens no activity, so there is nothing beneath the attempt for it to name.

lifecycleStreamStarted.description: A stream over `target` opened and is about to be iterated; construction alone emits nothing. `batchSize` is the positive page size the stream requests, which is what makes its Stream Batch children countable against a result the events never size.

lifecycleStreamFinished.description: The stream reached its terminal outcome. `exhausted` finishes at the moment exhaustion is discovered. `closedEarly` is a caller break, explicit close, caller exception, or cancellation before exhaustion, and rewrites no caller control flow. `failed` is reserved for Parallax's own planning, database, conversion, materialization, invalid-data, or cleanup work.

lifecycleFailure.description: How a failing outcome is attributed, applied to every transition carrying an Activity Failure. `attribution` is STATED rather than implied by the presence of `cause`, because which child a failure names — or that it names none — is the assertion, and an absent key would read as an unwritten one. `caused` names the DIRECT child this activity holds its one attribution for, so a cause is walked one link at a time rather than read off a single event, and a call that COMPLETED can be that child: attribution follows exception identity, never temporal proximity. `code` is the stable string the failing exception publishes as its own, absent for one publishing none. The qualified type, the message, and the stack are implementation-level and absent.

executionLifecycleObservation.description: The execution lifecycle a run delivered (m-execution-lifecycle), in the same shape the case's `then.executionLifecycle` oracle authors: the ordered Root Executions the run opened and each one's complete Started/Finished stream. A runner compares it structurally against the oracle, which is why the two shapes mirror each other rather than each choosing its own spelling. A Database Call names its statement by index into this envelope's own `emissions`.

graphs.description: The ordered per-milestone snapshot graphs produced by a history or asOfRange read, compared entry-for-entry with the case's then.graphs oracle.

tableState.description: Observed logical table state. Modeled scalar cells and declared document leaves use m-wire canonical output for their resolved declarations.

storedDataIssues.description: The stored-data diagnoses a read published for the result positions whose stored state contradicted the declared model (m-snapshot-read), compared against the case's `then.storedDataIssues`. Reported by an eager and a STREAMED graph-form read alike: a delivery classifies the same positions at the same ordinals its eager peer does, so the observation is the delivery's own rather than a second eager read's. Optional and additive — a conforming read publishes none and omits it, and existing run outputs stay valid.

stateChecks.description: Lifecycle-state checks (m-detach five-state machine) an adapter reports for scenario steps declaring `expectState`. Optional and additive — an adapter that reports no lifecycle state omits it, and existing run outputs stay valid.

stepRows.description: The values each scenario read step published (m-conformance-adapter), in step order, compared against each step's `expectRows`. A scenario has no single whole-read result, so these ride their own per-step key rather than the whole-read `rows` member. Optional and additive — a run reporting no such step omits it, and existing run outputs stay valid.

stepGraphs.description: The relationship contents an adapter observed at each scenario step declaring `expectGraph` (m-case-format), in step order. A scenario has no single whole-read graph, so these ride their own per-step key rather than the whole-read `graph` member. Optional and additive — a run whose case declares no `expectGraph` omits it, and existing run outputs stay valid.

errors.description: Neutral application-lifecycle errors (m-detach / m-identity-map / m-unit-work) an adapter reports for scenario steps declaring `expectError`. Optional and additive — an adapter that raises no such error omits it, and existing run outputs stay valid.

errorClass.description: The neutral `m-db-error` category the final trigger statement's raised failure classified to on an error-shape run, compared against the case's `then.errorClass`. Distinct from the application-lifecycle `errors` observation (which has no native-code witness). Optional and additive — only error-shape runs report it, and existing run outputs stay valid.

nativeCode.description: The preserved native code witness paired with `errorClass` (Postgres SQLSTATE string / MariaDB vendor errno integer), compared against the case's per-dialect `then.nativeCode`.

executionLifecycle.description: The transient execution lifecycle the run delivered (m-execution-lifecycle), compared against the case's `then.executionLifecycle`. Optional and additive — an adapter that installs no Provider omits it, and existing run outputs stay valid — but an adapter claiming `m-execution-lifecycle` MUST report it for every case authoring the oracle.

rejectedRule.description: The classified normative rule identifier a rejected-case run refused the input with (m-predicate / m-navigate / m-value-object / m-inheritance), compared against the case's `then.rejectedRule`. An adapter whose claim includes the `rejected` caseShape MUST report this observation on a rejected-case run, with `roundTrips: 0` and no provisioning or dialect. Optional and additive at the schema layer — only rejected-shape runs report it, and existing run outputs stay valid.

compileRunOnly.description: The defined `compile` answer for a CLAIMED case the corpus declares RUN-ONLY (`compileEligibility`, m-case-format). Its emissions cannot be derived without executing SQL, so the adapter neither compiles it (that would require running a query) nor returns `unsupported` (invalid for a claimed case command). Instead it returns `status: run-only` with at least one `compile-run-only` diagnostic; only the `run` command grades the case. Exit code 11.

allOf.description: At least one diagnostic MUST carry the reserved code `compile-run-only` naming the run-only reason.

runOk.description: A completed `run`. `profile` names the declared database matrix profile the case was run under; `dialect` is the dialect the adapter that profile opened actually executed the case in, which is what selects the per-dialect golden the emissions are compared against. The derivation runs one way only: a profile fixes its dialect by reading it back off the adapter it declares, while a dialect fixes no profile, because profiles may share one. Both are reported because a consumer of this envelope holds neither the roster nor that adapter.
